17c73475e41269b53ea60d454a4a676b5cf15064.summary: BlueHat v17 conference slide deck by Billy Leonard of the Threat Analysis Group (November 2017) on ten years of targeted credential phishing. It traces how attackers changed delivery, persistence and exfiltration, and how defenses evolved. Techniques named include two-factor bypass, SMS interception and OAuth abuse. Defenses named include Password Alert, security keys and the Advanced Protection Program. Much of the deck is slide titles and source lists, and some site boilerplate is not recorded.

17d3d0b4c787d59bcdc0a051c4f0fbe2e3d248e0.summary: Symantec reports on the Noberus ransomware, widely believed to succeed the Darkside and BlackMatter families from the Coreid group (FIN7). Noberus, first seen in November 2021 and written in Rust, is run as ransomware-as-a-service and is claimed to encrypt files on Windows, EXSI, Debian, ReadyNAS and Synology. The report covers 2022 updates, a new Exmatter data-theft tool, and the Eamfo infostealer that steals credentials stored by Veeam backup software. The FBI counted at least 60 compromised organisations between November 2021 and March 2022.

hedges: Noberus is widely believed to be a successor payload to the Darkside and BlackMatter ransomware families.
Coreid claims that Noberus is capable of encrypting files on Windows, EXSI, Debian, ReadyNAS, and Synology operating systems.
The ransomware being deployed by different affiliates can sometimes explain the different TTPs and attack chains used in Noberus attacks.
This was possibly a bid to avoid detection.
Whether Exmatter is the creation of Coreid or a skilled affiliate of the group is not clear.
Eamfo appears to have been in existence since at least August 2021.
Suggesting those behind Monti may be former affiliates of that group.
The number of victims now is likely to be many multiples of the FBI figure.
